state.case_summary:
An older woman with a history of diabetes and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation presented with sudden-onset chest pain. One hour later, the intensity of pain had increased.

Vital signs showed a normal heart rate and blood pressure initially. Later, her blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg without arrhythmia or bleeding.

- ECG findings:    At presentation: Normal sinus rhythm, up to 2.0-mm ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9, and 1.0-mm to 2.0-mm downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4. R/S greater than 1 in leads V1-V2.    One hour later: New ST-segment elevation in V5-6 and higher ST-segment elevation in inferior and posterior leads. No pathologic Q waves.  - Laboratory tests:    Initial high-sensitive troponin T level: 0.309 ng/mL (reference range, 0.00-0.03 ng/mL)  - Imaging studies:    1. Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery    2. Computer tomography angiography revealed contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Acute inferoposterolateral ST-elevation myocardial infarction
B. Cardiac tamponade due to ventricular wall rupture
C. Acute inferoposterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)
D. Subacute left ventricular free wall rupture (LVFWR) complicating acute myocardial infarction

root.label: Acute Chest Pain Syndrome with Suspected Ischaemic Aetiology and Cardiac Compromise
supporting_facts: ECG findings of ST-segment elevation in multiple leads
emergency angiography showing thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
computer tomography angiography revealing contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion
excluded_candidates: Pulmonary embolism: less likely due to the presence of ST-segment elevation and elevated troponin levels
Aortic dissection: unlikely due to the lack of aortic dilatation on imaging and the presence of coronary occlusion
salient_findings: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
ST-segment elevation in V5-6 and higher ST-segment elevation in inferior and posterior
elevated high-sensitive troponin T level of 0.309 ng/mL
thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
